Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 1) Powder is classified as a:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Powder is a solid dosage form. Tablet, capsule, pill and lozenge are also solid forms. Solid forms are commonly used for oral drug delivery.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 2) Ointment is classified as a:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Ointment is a semisolid dosage form. Cream, gel and paste are also semisolid preparations. They are commonly applied on skin or mucous membrane.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 3) Suspension is classified as a:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Suspension is a liquid dosage form. Solution, emulsion, drops, lotion, injection and liquid spray are also liquid forms. Suspension contains dispersed solid particles in liquid.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 4) Nebulizer belongs to which dosage-form group?
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Nebulizer is grouped under gaseous or inhalational forms. Aerosol, gas and metered-dose inhaler are also in this group. These forms are commonly used for respiratory drug delivery.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 5) Lozenge is best classified as:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Lozenge is a solid dosage form. It dissolves slowly in the mouth. It is commonly used for local action in throat or oral cavity.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 6) Gel is classified as:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Gel is a semisolid preparation. It has a jelly-like consistency. It is commonly used for topical application.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 7) Injection is classified as:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Injection is a liquid dosage form. It is given by parenteral routes. It bypasses gastrointestinal absorption when given intravenously.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 8) Metered-dose inhaler is classified as:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Metered-dose inhaler is an inhalational dosage form. It delivers a measured dose into the respiratory tract. It is commonly used in asthma and COPD treatment.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 9) Which group contains only solid dosage forms?
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Tablet, capsule, pill and lozenge are solid forms. They are usually administered orally. They differ in formulation and release characteristics.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 10) Which group contains only semisolid dosage forms?
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Ointment, cream, gel and paste are semisolid forms. They are usually applied externally. Their base affects absorption and skin suitability.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 11) Which group contains only liquid dosage forms?
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Solution, suspension, emulsion and drops are liquid forms. They differ by particle dispersion and uniformity. Liquid forms are useful when swallowing solids is difficult.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 12) Which group contains only inhalational forms?
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Aerosol, gas, nebulizer and MDI are inhalational forms. They deliver drugs to the respiratory tract. Some may also produce rapid systemic absorption.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 13) Compared with capsule, tablet usually has:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Tablets require excipients. Excipients help shape, bind, disintegrate or stabilize the preparation. Capsules may contain excipients but not always.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 14) Compared with tablet, capsule usually has:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Capsules usually have more rapid onset than tablets. Tablet absorption requires disintegration first. Capsule shell dissolves and releases drug more readily.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 15) Absorption of tablet requires:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Tablet must disintegrate before absorption. Disintegration breaks the tablet into smaller particles. This allows dissolution and later absorption.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 16) Disintegration is usually not needed for absorption of:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Capsule usually does not need tablet-like disintegration. Its shell dissolves and releases drug. That is why onset may be faster than tablet.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 17) Cream is mainly:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Cream is water-based. It is quickly absorbed by the skin. It is preferred for oily skin.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 18) Ointment is mainly:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Ointment is oil-based. It stays longer over the skin. It is useful in dry skin.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 19) Cream contains approximately:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Cream contains about 50% oil and 50% water. Its water-based nature makes it lighter. It is absorbed quickly.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 20) Ointment contains approximately:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Ointment contains about 80% oil and 20% water. It is more greasy than cream. It remains longer on the skin.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 21) Best topical preparation for oily skin is:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Cream is best for oily skin. It is water-based and quickly absorbed. It is less greasy than ointment.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 22) Best topical preparation for dry skin is:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Ointment is best for dry skin. It is oil-based and occlusive. It stays longer and reduces dryness.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 23) Best formulation for hairy skin is:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Lotion is best for hairy skin. It spreads easily between hairs. Thick ointment or paste may be difficult to apply.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 24) The topical preparation that remains longer on skin is:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Ointment remains longer over skin. Its oily base delays removal and absorption. It is useful when prolonged local contact is desired.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 25) The topical preparation quickly absorbed by skin is:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Cream is quickly absorbed by skin. It is water-based and less greasy. It is less suitable for very dry skin than ointment.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 26) A water-based topical preparation is:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Cream is water-based. It is lighter than ointment. It is useful when quick absorption is desired.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 27) An oil-based topical preparation is:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Ointment is oil-based. It contains a higher proportion of oil. It is better for dry skin.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 28) A preparation containing two immiscible liquids, one dispersed in another, is called:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Emulsion contains two immiscible liquids. One liquid is dispersed in the other. Oil-in-water and water-in-oil emulsions are common examples. Creams are often emulsion-based topical preparations.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 29) A preparation containing undissolved solid particles dispersed in a liquid is:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Suspension contains solid particles dispersed in liquid. It usually needs shaking before use. The drug is not fully dissolved. Dose uniformity depends on proper dispersion before administration.

Drug Formulation and doses form.question: 30) A preparation in which drug is completely dissolved in liquid is:
Drug Formulation and doses form.exp: Solution is a homogeneous liquid preparation. The drug is completely dissolved in solvent. It does not require shaking for uniformity like suspension. It usually gives more uniform dosing than suspension.
